title: Microsoft Purview: Azure PST Import to Exchange Online mailboxes (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's supplied notice, including the April 2027 rollout and administrator-driven workflow. The Azure role-assignment path, automation and storage meters are supported; feature-specific licensing and cmdlet documentation remain unpublished in the sources checked.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn page for the new Azure PST Import workflow was found at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Azure PST Import"; "Azure PST Import" PowerShell cmdlet licensing pricing. Opened pst-import-overview and New-MigrationEndpoint; results describe the existing portal import or other migration methods, not this new workflow.

claims.claim: Learn documents an existing network-upload PST import method in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Network upload: Upload the PST files over the network to a temporary Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud.

claims.claim: Learn also documents drive shipping for the existing PST import service.
claims.quote: Drive shipping: Copy the PST files to a BitLocker-encrypted hard drive and then physically ship the drive to Microsoft.

claims.claim: The existing portal-based method uses a PST import job in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Create a PST import job on the Import PST files page in the Microsoft Purview portal and submit the PST import mapping file you created in the previous step.

claims.claim: The Azure portal route through the storage account's IAM role assignments, role selection and service-principal member selection supports the printed path.
claims.quote:
Click Access control (IAM).
Click the Role assignments tab to view the role assignments at this scope.
Click Add > Add role assignment.
On the Members tab, select User, group, or service principal

claims.claim: az role assignment create supports the printed --role, --assignee-object-id, --assignee-principal-type and storage-account --scope arguments.
claims.quote:
az role assignment create \
    --role "Storage Blob Data Reader" \
    --assignee-object-id "aaaaaaaa-0000-1111-2222-bbbbbbbbbbbb" \
    --assignee-principal-type "User"

claims.claim: Assigning the Azure role requires Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write permissions at the corresponding scope or higher.
claims.quote: To run the command, you must have a role that includes Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write permissions assigned to you at the corresponding scope or higher.

claims.claim: Azure storage role-assignment changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: When you assign roles or remove role assignments, it can take up to 10 minutes for changes to take effect.

claims.claim: The supplied notice does not name the PowerShell cmdlets for Azure PST Import.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete supplied MC1455013 notice for cmdlet names; it refers to PowerShell cmdlets, an endpoint creation cmdlet and detailed cmdlet usage, but gives no cmdlet name.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Learn cmdlet or parameter documenting this new Azure PST Import workflow was found in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Azure PST" "New-MigrationEndpoint"; "Azure PST Import" "New-MigrationBatch" Analyze. Read both references and New-MailboxImportRequest excerpts. PSTImport is on-premises/internal only; no parameter documents the announced Azure PST Import workflow.

claims.claim: The notice names no Exchange or Purview administrator role required to run the cmdlets.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1455013 in full for Exchange and Purview execution roles. It names administrator access to PowerShell cmdlets and Storage Blob Data Reader for the app, but no Exchange or Purview admin role for cmdlet execution.

claims.claim: The supplied records do not explain how the notice's Global rollout maps to the roadmap's government clouds.
claims.quote: Searched: read MC1455013 rollout and audience sections alongside roadmap 565865 cloud fields. The notice says Global; the record lists GCC, GCC High and DoD, without an explanation mapping the two.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The admin-opt-in default is supported by a workflow that requires administrators to configure an endpoint and explicitly run the import.
claims.quote: The process starts by creating an Azure PST Import endpoint to establish the connection between Azure storage and Exchange Online. Administrators then run a migration batch in Analyze mode to review readiness and validate the input before proceeding.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated a default beyond the administrator-driven workflow in the supplied sources.
claims.quote: Searched: "Azure PST Import" license price documentation cmdlets roles default; read roadmap 565865, MC1455013 and pst-import-overview. No default for the new feature beyond the administrator-run workflow was found.
